Subject: DPA intake: request for Redwood DPA + subprocessor disclosures

Hi Priyom,

We are preparing for a security review ahead of our pilot and need two things to move forward on our side:

1) Redwood's current DPA template and any notes on which clauses are negotiable (specifically: data retention, breach notification timing, and liability caps).
2) A current list of subprocessors (name, role, country) and whether any subprocessors process data outside the US/EU.

We also need to understand your default cross-border transfer mechanism for EU personal data (standard contractual clauses, adequacy, or other). Our legal team will want to confirm.

Can you send the materials and let me know your expected turnaround for review? We are aiming to have a signed DPA before the end of Q1 2027 for procurement gating.

Thanks,

Thanks for the clear ask. Attaching our current DPA template and the latest subprocessor register. Quick notes up front:

- Attachment 1 (Redwood_Standard_DPA_v1.4.pdf): our baseline DPA. We generally accept limited redlines to sections on data subject rights, SCPs for transfers, and operational security.
- Attachment 2 (Redwood_Subprocessors_202611.pdf): current list (name / role / country). We highlight a small set that operate in APAC and EU.

Next steps we propose:
1) You circulate any initial redlines/issues after an internal review.
2) I loop in Laura Bennett (cc'd) from Legal and Neha Kapoor from Privacy to resolve legal/transfer questions.
3) If redlines are light, we can route to DocuSign for signature; otherwise Legal will propose tracked changes.

I can turn around clarifying answers within 1 business day and have Legal review redlines within 2-3 business days depending on complexity.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Tom and I will review and flag anything else.

Hi Allison,

Thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. A few points from Legal & Privacy:

- Breach notification: we can agree to 24-hour initial notification for incidents that meet your materiality threshold; our incident response includes provisional notifications and we will follow up with a detailed report.
- Audit rights: Redwood primarily provides SOC 2 Type II reports and we can grant a limited, scoped right to audit for PHI-processing customers through a cooperative review process. We can also provide exportable logs for specific incidents or requests (subject to mutual NDAs).
- Encryption/KMS: our default is Redwood-managed keys with tenant-level encryption. For enterprise customers with regulatory needs, we offer Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) via supported KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS) — we can document the technical flow.

I'll attach a short implementation summary for how we operationalize SCCs and key controls (Redwood_SCC_implementation_summary.pdf). If acceptable, Priyom can prepare a DocuSign envelope with the agreed DPA so you can sign and we can attach the SCCs as an appendix.

If you'd like a quick call to confirm the BYOK timeline and responsibilities, Neha and I are available Wed 11:00–12:00 PST.

Regards,
